title: 54% of US Workers Skip Lunch at Least Once a Week
paragraphs: Lunch is an important meal. But many workers in the US do not eat it every day.

A company called ezCater does a survey about lunch every year. ezCater helps businesses order food for their workers. This year, it asked 1,000 people who work full-time in the US about their lunch habits.

The survey found that 54% of workers skip lunch at least once a week. This means that more than half of workers do not eat lunch at all on some days. This number has gone up for four years in a row. In 2025, it was 51%. In 2023, it was 48%.
Also, only 36% of workers leave their desks for lunch every workday. Many people eat at their desks while they work.

Why do people skip lunch? There are a few reasons. Many workers are very busy and have a lot of meetings. Some people feel pressure at work. Food is also more expensive than before. In fact, workers are spending less money on lunch. In 2026, they spent about $100 a week on lunch. That is 8% less than in 2025.
Many workers also eat alone. About 62% of people said they eat alone when they are at their workplace.
Experts say skipping lunch is not good for workers. Without food, people can feel tired and find it hard to focus. A lunch break can also give people time to rest and talk with their coworkers.
